Metadata.description: Compose circuit boards and devices in 3D, simulate them and see instantly whether every component will work.
Metadata.imageAlt: The Echidna home page: “Know it works before you build it.” beside a 3D development board with all checks passed.

hero.eyebrow: A 3D studio for circuit boards and devices
hero.lead: Place parts, swap them and see straight away whether every component stays within its limits. Built for makers, students and anyone curious about what is inside their devices.

demo.title: Try a swap
demo.caption: A 5 V supply, a series resistor and a red LED. Choose a smaller resistor and watch the current climb.
demo.diagramLabel: Circuit: 5 V supply, series resistor and LED in a single loop
demo.explainPass: The LED draws {current} mA, comfortably under its {rating} mA rating.
demo.explainWarn: The LED is at {percent} of its rating. It will light, but there is no headroom left.
demo.explainFail: The LED would draw {current} mA against a {rating} mA rating. It will overheat and fail early.
demo.note: Simplified here with a fixed 2 V LED drop. The studio solves the full circuit.

checks.heading: Every part passes three checks
checks.lead: A component only fits a slot when all three agree. If one fails, Echidna tells you which and by how much.

connects.title: It connects
connects.body: The interface matches: the right socket, connector and number of lanes.

powered.title: It is powered
powered.body: The slot’s rails can supply the voltage and current the part needs.

cool.title: It stays cool
cool.body: The heat it gives off fits the slot’s thermal budget and the cooling around it.

devices.heading: Six kinds of device, one set of rules
devices.lead: Recreate a real device from a preset or start from a blank board. Each type has its own catalogue of swappable parts.

provenance.heading: Every number shows where it came from
provenance.lead: Values are labelled as datasheet, teardown or estimate, so you know how far to trust a verdict. When a fail rests only on estimates, Echidna says it is likely to fail rather than certain.

cta.heading: Start with a blank board
cta.body: Open the studio, pick a part from the library and see its verdict as you place it.

assembly.label: Development board with every part in place; pressing the power button lights each part in turn as power reaches it

swap.heading: Change one part, see the verdict
swap.lead: Every swap is checked the moment you make it. Try it here with the simplest circuit there is.

devices.label: Device types
devices.body: Phones, PCs, laptops, drones, dev boards and wearables.

checks.label: Checks per part
checks.body: Connection, power and heat, every time you place a part.

sources.label: Data sources
sources.body: Every value is labelled datasheet, teardown or estimate.

languages.label: Languages
languages.body: In light and dark themes, in the browser, with nothing to install.

languages.heading: Speaks your language
languages.lead: Every label, verdict and explanation, in seven languages.

reasons.unwired: One of its leads isn’t wired, so no current can flow through it.
reasons.shorted: Both leads are wired to the same net, so current goes around the LED instead of through it.
reasons.reversed: It’s wired backwards: the cathode sits at a higher voltage than the anode.
reasons.open: No current flows through it: the circuit isn’t a closed loop, or the voltage is too low to light it.

switchOn.title: After switch-on
switchOn.span: Shown over the first {time}, by when it has settled.
switchOn.unsettled: Still changing after {time}; it takes longer than that to settle.
switchOn.hint: Point at the plots, or focus them and use the arrow keys, to replay switch-on on the board.
switchOn.instant: Nothing in this circuit stores energy, so it reaches these values the moment it is switched on.
switchOn.failed: Couldn’t simulate switch-on for this circuit. Check for parts with extreme values, such as a capacitor far larger than intended.

errors.singular: This circuit can’t be solved. Check for supplies wired directly across each other.
errors.noConvergence: The solver couldn’t settle on an answer for this circuit.
errors.invalidValue: {id} has a value the solver can’t use.
errors.internal: Something went wrong while solving. Try the change again.

Studio.simulateOn: Live: every change is solved and checked. Select to pause.
Studio.simulateOff: Paused. Select to solve and check changes live.

voltageRating.name: Voltage rating
voltageRating.explain: The voltage across this part is {percent} of its rating. Keep it below 80% for a safety margin; above 100% the part can break down.

currentRating.name: Current rating
currentRating.explain: This part is carrying {percent} of the most current it is rated for. Above 80% it runs hot and wears out sooner; above 100% it can fail.

powerRating.name: Power rating
powerRating.explain: This part is turning {percent} of its rated power into heat. Above 80% it gets hot; above 100% it can burn out.

temperatureRating.name: Temperature
temperatureRating.explain: This part is estimated to use {percent} of the temperature rise it can take above the surrounding air. Above 80% it ages faster; above 100% it can be damaged. Less power through the part, or one with a higher power rating, keeps it cooler.

switchOnVoltage.name: Voltage at switch-on
switchOnVoltage.explain: Just after switch-on, the voltage across this part briefly reaches {percent} of its rating, more than it settles to. Ringing between an inductor and a capacitor can do this; more resistance in the loop calms it.

switchOnCurrent.name: Current at switch-on
switchOnCurrent.explain: While the circuit starts up, this part carries {percent} of its rated current for a millisecond or more, usually while a large capacitor charges. A smaller capacitor or more series resistance shortens the surge.

switchOnPower.name: Heat at switch-on
switchOnPower.explain: While the circuit starts up, this part turns {percent} of its rated power into heat for a millisecond or more, usually while a large capacitor charges. A smaller capacitor or more series resistance shortens the surge.

psuBudget.name: PSU power budget
psuBudget.explain: The build draws {percent} of the PSU’s rated output at full load. Above 80% leaves little headroom for spikes; above 100% the PSU can shut down or fail.

powerConnectors.name: PSU connectors
powerConnectors.explain: The parts need {percent} of the connectors the PSU has of one type. Above 100% something can’t be plugged in.

cooling.name: Cooling
cooling.explain: The processors give off {percent} of the heat the cooler is rated to remove. Above 90% they run hot under load; above 100% they slow themselves down to stay safe.

chargerBudget.name: Charger power
chargerBudget.explain: At full load the laptop draws {percent} of what the charger supplies. Above 100% the battery makes up the difference and drains even while plugged in; above 150% it can’t keep up under load.
